This post is meant to be a breakdown of terms, a legend of sorts on what is meant when terms are used. Please see this list for discussion points. If the meaning you are intending is different than listed here: Please track down the specific term. This is to clarify and lubricate communication, not to act as some sort of bible.

Most political terms have multiple meanings. Many are applied to specific vectors of application or change by region. Case in point, in the US "Neo-Conservatism" meaning one who advocates a sort of extreme corporate freedom and market freedom at expense of individuals, is referred to "Neo-Liberalism" in Europe and other parts of the world. The US tends to favor social meaning over economic, so some things are simply different. Since I suspect most users of this Sub will be from the America's I will focus on terms specific to that region. The terms contained in this are SIMPLIFIED. As with everything, exceptions exist. This is meant as the baseline.

Liberal : Someone who advocates the freedom of the individual and governmental guarantees of individual rights and liberties. Often the distinction of Liberal vs. Libertarian is the role of the government. Liberals view the role of the government to ensure personal freedoms and mediate any conflicts internally. Oft times Liberalism is conflated with Progressivism. Sort of a left wing version of Libertarian. The Progressivism of pre WW2 intermingled with Liberal ideals to create the modern form of Liberalism.

Libertarian : Someone who advocates the freedom of the individual and sees the government as a limiting factor on that personal freedom. Sort of a right wing version of Liberal.

Progressive : Someone who advocates political and or societal reform based on the notion of 'progress'. In the US, the primary focus of Progressives in the past decade has been on societal concerns (equality, equity). Extreme left, counterpart to Conservative. Initial focus was economic, the Progressive period rose around 1900, but died out after WW2. It's economic focus moved into left form Liberalism. Todays "Progressive" movement is almost entirely focused on perceived social injustice.

Conservative : At it's base, it is simply someone who advocates restraint. In economics this restraint can be budget controls or social. Social conservatives are primarily focused on traditional aspects of society. Extreme right, counterpart to Progressive.

Social Justice : Practitioners are pejoratively called SJW's (Social Justice Warriors). Often employ arguments based on Post-Modernist philosophies wherein a 'sin' is identified and evidence to show guilt of sing sought after. Contrarian evidence is regarded as positive evidence. SJW's intersect with Feminism. This sub regards SJW stances as a form of Political Cultism.

Dominionism : Extreme right wing conservative ideology. Many political evangelicals fit into this group. The ideology is "God" has granted them dominion over the world and they cannot stray from the will. Any act they do is blessed by "God" and is his will to allow them to take power. This sub regards Dominionism as a form of Political Cultism.

Political Cultism : Any ideology that relies upon feelings as the basis of the claim. Usually typified by a focus on 'sin' and Ad Hominem attacks. A political cultist will usually respond to any challenge to their ideology with overt hostility, regards the source of the subject points over the evidence provided etc..

Capitalism : Though technically in politics Capitalism means a series of laws to benefit those that control capital-and by extension the flow of capital for benefit of economy. It is typically phrased as a sort of individual right of self destiny. For purposes of discussion Capitalism should be limited to economic enterprise of non-governmental entities. An individual is not a capitalist unless they work with capital, or large finances. The ideology is credited with fostering competition and through that advancement in various sectors. If taken to extremes, capitalism leads to Oligarchy and Fascism. The term is often regarded as a 'sin' topic.

Socialism : In political theory, socialism is laws meant to benefit society. Practical applications are meant to benefit the society. If taken to extremes it leads to Communism.

Communism : Extreme form of Socialism in which the government takes over all roles and presents them as benefit to all. The mantra "From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs." is a common slogan in Communism. Though it is often seen as noble in it's own right, likewise used as a 'sin', Communism has not had a successful run and appears to lead towards decay. If people have no reason to strive, the populace becomes sedentary, it also relies on an authoritarian form of government.

Fascism : Political theory has specific meaning for this, often people use the term to mean 'authoritarian' and or 'tyrannical', however, fascism is the premise that the most successful should rule. It rose in Mussolini's Italy. A sort of Darwinism applied to leadership. Oligarchic in basis with the most successful businessmen determining policy to be replaced when a new 'cream' rises to the top. It is typified by the division of the 'haves' and 'have nots'. Those who are not in the successful caste are regarded as resources to be used as the leaders see fit. However, it manifests as nationalism with expected sacrifices on the individual. The tenets of Fascism involve conquest and a 'might is right' mentality merged with nationalism.

Socialism is to Communism, what Capitalism is to Fascism. Though jingoistic is a reasonable phrasing.

The primary goal of this sub is to combat political cultists regardless of the political axis they are on.

More will come as time allows.
